# Public virtual execution paths

**Generated by bin/generate_bindings.py from bindings/manifest.json; do not edit.** Domain classification: `bin/callback-matrix` and `upstream/callback-rules.json`.

All **434 public virtual declarations**, including deprecated overloads, destructors and value virtuals.
The denominator is unchanged. No entry is promoted to verified by this report.

**Laboratory means explicitly enabled, offline and main-thread only, never Rack's engine/driver threads.**
See [Callbacks and the laboratory](../explanation/callbacks.md) for restrictions, fidelity gaps and
re-entrant dispatch (fixed by `tk-rackpy-trampolines-suppress-same-object-re-entra-0abce9`).
Native configured/queued driver adapters are production paths; their synchronous Python paths are the
laboratory drivers and devices of RP-22F (`tk-rackpy-22f-laboratory-python-paths-for-audio-and-65ccf3`). A callable name is not proof of an override.
No plugin can subclass Rack's Scene, RackScrollWidget or RackWidget (PRIVATE constructors) or make a usable PlugWidget subclass, so their UI virtuals map to calls on Rack's own instances through borrowed host views (RP-28F decision, owner-approved 2026-10-26: `tk-rackpy-28f-python-subclass-trampolines-for-plugw-154b61`).
Per-symbol semantics below retain the manifest's adapter restrictions; implemented is not verified.

## Execution domains

| Domain | Legitimate Rack execution domain |
| --- | --- |
| `ui` | Main (UI) thread with no engine lock held. A Python override may run; the trampoline takes the GIL. |
| `ui-exclusive` | Main thread, or whichever thread called the engine method, while Rack holds the engine mutex EXCLUSIVELY and audio processing is stopped. A Python override may run, but must not call any engine method that locks (RackPy refuses it), and its run time stalls audio. |
| `ui-shared` | Main thread while Rack holds the engine mutex SHARED, so process() keeps running concurrently. A Python override may run synchronously, but must read module state through atomics or snapshots, never through fields that process() writes. |
| `engine` | Engine worker or fallback threads during processing. Production: native code only. Python only in the separately enabled RP-22 laboratory. |
| `driver` | Audio or MIDI driver threads (and, for some, the engine thread or UI under the exclusive lock). Native code only; Python receives queued notifications on the UI thread. |
| `mixed` | Reachable from both the UI thread and engine threads. Native implementation only; Python may configure the native behaviour but never runs in the call. |
| `lifecycle` | Destructor: runs on the thread that deletes the object, which Rack keeps on the main thread for widgets and modules. Trampolines release their Python state with the GIL there; production deletion paths do no Python work. |
| `unresolved` | Not yet decided. Blocks the implementation task named in the rule. |
| `value` | Not a callback: a virtual on a C++ exception or value type. RackPy translates or wraps it; Python never overrides it. |
